inputs.xtext_rule_text:
TargetSuccession returns SysML::SuccessionAsUsage :
	ownedRelationship += MultiplicitySourceEndMember
	'then' ownedRelationship += ConnectorEndMember
;

notes: re-scoped from the shared unit to sysml alone (ADR-0015)
decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.8. The Xtext accepts the same tokens and differs only in the name of the first member: it writes MultiplicitySourceEndMember, whose MultiplicitySourceEnd is `{SysML::ReferenceUsage} ( ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity )?` (SysML.xtext:883-888), and the clause writes SourceEndMember, whose SourceEnd is `( ownedRelationship += OwnedMultiplicity )?` (8.2.2.9.3). Those are the same production under two names, so this is a naming difference rather than a disagreement, and the clause's name is taken because only SourceEndMember has a unit. The source end carries no reference of its own — at most a multiplicity — which is what makes this the target form: the source is the body item the succession follows, and only the target is written.

evidence.note: States the production; the rule is its transcription.

Inside `action def MonitoredActivity {` on line 8: line 12 `then performCriticalActivity;` and line 13 `then waitForTimeOut;` are each a bare 'then' followed by a reference and a ';' — this production, with the ';' belonging to the enclosing ActionTargetSuccession's UsageBody. Line 21 and line 24 `then stop;` are the same shape.
Second opinion. Same tokens; its MultiplicitySourceEndMember (883) is the clause's SourceEndMember under another name.
